**Second measured observation — PR-body footer under a raw REST `PATCH /pulls`** (skills seat, 2026-09-04T06:55Z; for the third platform-readings increment ruled here).

Surface: PR https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15073, body edited by the #15061 dev (branch `claude/issue-15061-catalog-gates-scan-references`) with a raw REST PATCH and a full read-back, 22,533 characters compared.

- The session-URL footer block (`_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_…)_`) **survived the edit verbatim**.
- A bare footer block (`_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`) was **appended under it**, leaving two blocks; everything else came back byte-identical.

This matches the first observation already recorded on #14133 for the same channel (REST PATCH appends a bare footer, +58 bytes, and leaves a session-URL footer intact; the MCP `update_pull_request` PATCH is the channel that deletes the block). It diverges from the AGENTS.md clause that says every PATCH normalises a session-URL footer down to bare — that clause describes the MCP channel, not REST. Two independent observations on the REST channel now agree; the AGENTS.md wording is a candidate correction for the increment this card rules on, not an edit from here (governed surface).

The next write, after compacting the body to 37,055 chars, came back identical with the footer intact.

Reading, scoped: on the issue-body edit end the platform leaves a bare footer alone up to at least 65,236 chars and dropped it once at 65,783 chars (n=1 at that size; the boundary between the two is unmeasured, and 65,536 sits inside it). Consequence for seats: a seat post approaching ~65k chars must compact into a body revision before the next write, and a read-back that is a strict prefix of what was sent, 58 chars short, is this shape — not sanitizer damage and not a reason to re-paste.
